speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please describe the onset of these symptoms and if the skin lesions are itchy or painful.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with Differential, ESR, CRP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL. ESR: Not available. CRP: Not available.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That diagnosis of iron deficiency anemia does not fit your symptoms of fever, chills, and violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists; could you tell me how long you have had these skin lesions and if you have any history of tick bites or recent travel to endemic areas?

REQUEST TEST: Blood Culture, Rheumatoid Factor, Anti-CCP.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_scan of wrist lesions.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_Cultures: Findings 'Pending at the time of examination'; Rheumatoid_Factor: Not available; Anti-CCP: Not available. Dermatology_scan: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cat Scratch Disease (Bacillary Angiomatosis).

The presence of painless, violaceous, vesiculopustular lesions specifically located on the wrists and hands, combined with systemic symptoms like fever and chills, is highly characteristic of this condition, often associated with cat exposure. While blood cultures are pending, the specific clinical presentation overrides the previous suggestion of iron deficiency anemia. Do you have any history of contact with cats or cats with open sores?
